findings.trigger_condition: Edge stream contains equal nodes where one is hashable and the other is unhashable but equal via __eq__ (e.g., frozenset({1,2}) and set({1,2}), or 1 and custom hashable vs unhashable equal). Call dependency_layers([(1, frozenset({1,2})), (1, {1,2})]) or [(frozenset({1}), 'a'), ({1}, 'b')].
findings.root_cause: _id_of splits identity into two disjoint registries: hashable values go to hash_buckets (dict keyed by value) and unhashable values go to unhashable_ids/unhashable_nodes linear list. The hashable path (line 42) uses dict lookup which requires hashability, and the unhashable except path (lines 44-45) only scans the unhashable list. Neither path cross-checks the other registry for equality (set == frozenset is True). Thus equal values across hashability boundary receive distinct ids.
findings.impact: Node deduplication fails: same logical node appears as two distinct ids. This creates spurious extra nodes in output layers, inflates indegree counts, breaks deduplication of repeated edges (seen_edges uses ids), and can cause incorrect layer ordering or incorrect cycle vs acyclic verdict. Violates contract to deduplicate repeated edges and include each node once ordered by first appearance.
findings.suggested_validation: Run edges = [(1, frozenset({1,2})), (1, set([1,2]))]; layers = dependency_layers(edges); assert len(layers[0]) == 1 and layers[0][0] == frozenset({1,2}) and layers == [[frozenset({1,2})],[1]] ; also test [(frozenset({1}), 'a'), (set({1}), 'b')] should yield single dependency node in first layer, not two. Reproduce failure shows two nodes in first layer.

findings.trigger_condition: Input contains many distinct unhashable nodes (e.g., 5000+ distinct list objects as nodes/dependencies) yielding an acyclic chain or star graph.
findings.root_cause: Unhashable registry is a flat list scanned linearly on every _id_of call (lines 44-45: for idx, candidate in zip(unhashable_ids, unhashable_nodes): if candidate is value or candidate == value). No hashing or indexing; each insertion/lookup is O(U) where U is number of distinct unhashable nodes. For N distinct unhashable nodes total cost is O(N^2) comparisons.
findings.impact: Quadratic time and CPU blowup on large unhashable graphs; violates implicit efficiency expectation and can cause timeouts/OOM on very deep or wide acyclic inputs that should be handled linearly. Deep acyclic chain of list-nodes will not recurse but will still be O(N^2).
findings.suggested_validation: Generate edges = [([i], [i+1]) for i in range(5000)] (distinct lists) and time dependency_layers(edges); profile shows ~12.5M equality checks. Compare against hashable equivalent with tuples ([(i,)]) which is O(N). Assert runtime scales linearly, not quadratically.
